text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- More than 130 people were killed -- most of them burned to death in a fire at a shopping mall -- during riots on Friday in the South Kalimantan capital of Banjarmasin in the worst outburst of violence in Indonesia's 27-day campaign leading up to the May 29 general election.
- Two crewmen died and three were injured after a fire broke out on board a 4,000-tonne oil tanker on Sunday morning.

- The Government is considering extending the hours of the Park and Ride Scheme, to encourage more motorists to switch to alternative modes of transport, said Minister of State for Communications John Chen.

- British government scientists are warning airlines that cosmic radiation from deep space could cripple computer systems on airlines while they are in flight, according to a report in the Internet edition of The Sunday Times.

- The Monetary Authority of Singapore is tightening up on risky index and currency-linked investment products by asking commercial banks to raise the minimum investment sum substantially, banking sources said.

- Indian tobacco giant ITC Ltd and the Singapore judicial managers of its troubled international trading operation, ITC Global Holdings, are moving towards a settlement despite ITC's recent disclaimer on legal liabilities, sources said.
- The collapse of a planned mega-merger between cash-strapped Thai finance firm Finance One and Thai Danu Bank ensures a rocky week ahead for Thailand's financial markets, analysts said.
- Prices of 16-megabit dynamic random access memory chips have eased by some 10 percent from their 1997 high in March, but there are signs that prices are stabilising.
- Local banks could disclose more financial information, says Development Bank of Singapore's president, Ng Kee Choe.
- Recent intervention by some Asian central banks to defend their currencies did little to reassure disaffected institutional investors, who continue to avoid the region.

- The widespread belief that private enterprise can make a major contribution to meeting Asia's huge needs for power, transport, communications and other forms of basic infrastructure needs to be radically rethought, a Japanese official working group has warned.
- Thailand's market for initial public offers has virtually dried up with eight companies having cancelled plans for IPOs.
- Thai Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan moved on Sunday to ease fears of a stocks plunge following the collapse of merger plans that were aimed at bailing out Thailand's largest finance firm.
